analysis: Examined the provider-release.md changes. Base 577-578 became head 577-579: a new step computes cluster runtime facts. The payload gains an optional `cluster_runtime` field (head 602-610, pinned platform df61dd6f; strict parse; DisallowUnknownFields on old coordinators). The new Cluster Runtime Facts section is head 649-795. Controls documented: secret-derived env values are removed and the signing keychain is deleted, with verification, before release code runs. Archive hash is checked against BUNDLE_HASH. The CLI runs under env -i. The catalog/CDN manifest/config fetch reads no weights. Validate enforces 128-byte IDs and the 64 KiB body limit. Per-environment opt-in variables gate the block; unset leaves the payload byte-identical. Catalog bounds are 64/64/256, with older releases dropped first. Main concern, recorded as a finding: release registration now derives public cluster authorization without independent approval. This affects A-017/TB-011 and is absent from the threat model. Unverified, for integration/platform review: coordinator derivation semantics (NativeRuntimeCatalogWithReleases, ParseReleaseClusterRuntime). Also unverified: whether evicting older releases' approvals strands deployed pairs (availability, T-057-like). Also whether catalog `input_modalities` fetched over the network can widen media admission, and whether later steps (prepare/registration) run with secrets after executing release-built code. test.md unit 13 (head 2308-2529) is test-documentation prose about cluster TP prefix records, media ingress, MTP and stop ordering. It changes no controls. The changed ranges of test.md (1289, 1325-1356: new test-script references) are orientation only; no regression found there. T-041 prefix record tests are synthetic and change no cache policy.

findings.detail: The new Cluster Runtime Facts flow (head lines 649-668) makes `POST /v1/releases` carry `cluster_runtime`. A coordinator derives that build's cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and public-traffic parity qualifications from it. The model list comes from the build's own `ClusterPublicModels` declaration and qualification records. The doc states that no operator posts approvals, grants or public qualifications per build. It also says qualifications apply to each declared family on any Apple silicon pair: "the declared placement names the evidence, not a limit." This removes a separate human approval for public cluster serving. Holding the release key (A-005) plus repository write access becomes enough to obtain public routing. A-017 instead describes qualifications as independently approved, separate from release publication. Trigger: a build whose source adds a model to `ClusterPublicModels`, or a catalog/CDN entry that changes `input_modalities`, would gain public pair routing and media admission on the next release with the variable on. That pair could be untested hardware. The threat model (TB-011, A-016/A-017, T-054, T-056) has no entry for cluster approvals or this derivation. Fix: add a threat entry for release-derived cluster authorization, its trust inputs (self-declared list, catalog/CDN metadata) and the bounds/eviction behavior. Alternatively, keep an independent approval gate for public qualification and limit qualifications to the evidenced hardware.
findings.title: Release registration now self-derives cluster approvals, serving grants and public parity qualifications
